hook_text: Diagram in one hand, crocodile clips in the other. Here is how to build any circuit right the first time, and draw any circuit you are handed.
clip_script: Read the whole diagram: supply, parts, right-way-round parts, trace the loop, no shortcuts. Lay the parts out like the drawing. Connect one lead at a time, switch open, plus round to minus. Check against the drawing, then close. Dead? Loose clip or flat cell, nine times in ten. Now four circuits: switch and lamp, a torch; push switch and buzzer, a doorbell and the heart of a panic button; motor, swap the leads and it reverses; resistor and LED, never without the resistor. Then two lamps in series: both dim, both die together. Two in parallel: both bright, one survives alone, battery works twice as hard. To draw a circuit, follow the wire from plus, a dot where it branches, rejoin with another dot, ignore where things sit. Hand it to a partner to build; if theirs behaves like yours, you drew it right.
visual_style: Whiteboard bench with parts arranged to mirror a diagram above; leads connect one by one; two lamps dim in series then brighten in parallel; a finger follows a wire and a diagram draws itself with dots at junctions.
pacing: Six steps, troubleshooting, four circuits, series versus parallel, drawing back.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build two lamps in series, then in parallel, and write what changed.
